speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have knee pain after increasing your physical activity; to help me narrow this down, how would you describe the specific location and nature of the pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail. Since the pain started yesterday with repetitive pivoting during volleyball, is the swelling localized to the kneecap (patella) or more diffuse around the knee joint? Also, does the pain improve when you rest completely?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)
